title: Panchavati
hook: a cold winter dawn by the river, and a brother says one sentence too many

segments.voice: Yesterday: Jatayu promised to guard Sita, and Lakshmana built the hut by the Godavari. A brother builds a house with his hands.

Time passes at Panchavati, and the season turns to hemanta, early winter. One morning before sunrise, the three of them walk down to the Godavari to bathe. Lakshmana carries the water pot, and he talks, the way people do on cold walks. Mist over the fields. The sun weak and far away. Water so cold, he says, that even the elephants touch it with their trunks and pull back.
screen: `HEMANTA: THE COLD SEASON.` → `A WALK TO THE RIVER AT DAWN.` → `EVEN THE ELEPHANTS PULL BACK.`

segments.voice: Then Lakshmana's mind goes home. Right now, he says, Bharata is probably walking down to the Sarayu in this same cold. He could be living in a palace. Instead he sleeps on the ground and keeps an ascetic's vows, out of love for you. Then he adds one sentence too many. How could a mother like Kaikeyi have a son like Bharata? Rama stops him. Don't speak badly of our middle mother, he says. Speak only of Bharata. And he says how much he misses him: Bharata's kind words, Rama says, come back to him like nectar. He longs to see him, and Shatrughna, and all of them. Rama lost a kingdom to Kaikeyi's wish, and he's the one who won't allow the bitterness. He doesn't argue that she was right. He just won't let the talk turn sour. Now the week. Viradha, the giant who was a cursed musician. Sharabhanga, who waited to see Rama before going to heaven, and the bones that brought Rama's promise. Sita's question about weapons, and Rama's answer. Agastya, who digested a demon and gave Rama a god's bow. Jatayu's offer to guard Sita. And Panchavati: a hut, a brother's handiwork, and a cold morning where blame is stopped at the door. This quiet is about to end.
screen: `BHARATA IN THE SAME COLD.` · `HOW COULD SHE HAVE SUCH A SON?` · `SPEAK ONLY OF BHARATA.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `BLAME STOPPED AT THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: Feel the breath come in a little cool through the nose and leave warm. Think of someone you've been tempted to complain about, then bring to mind someone connected to them whom you love or admire. Rest your attention on the good one, breathing in cool and out warm.
Panchavati. A winter dawn by the Godavari, where Rama tells Lakshmana: don't speak badly of our middle mother. Speak of Bharata.
Your line: speak only of Bharata. Tomorrow, the quiet breaks. A week deeper into the forest, done.

screen: `DAY 560 COUNTS.` → `A WEEK DEEPER INTO THE FOREST, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: SHURPANAKHA.`

howItsDone: Some Hindu teachers cite Rama's refusal to let Lakshmana speak ill of Kaikeyi as an example of restraint in speech within a family.

original.note: Sanskrit hemanta: the early-winter season, one of the traditional seasons of the Indian year.

trapdoor: what you thought: Panchavati is where nothing much happens.
what it means: in the quiet, Rama refuses to let blame settle on Kaikeyi.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 16 is a famous season poem that turns into a lesson on speech: Rama silences blame and turns to praise.

chat.says: Lakshmana was only criticizing Kaikeyi, who caused the exile. Why did Rama stop him?
options: Rama wouldn't let blame settle on their middle mother, and turned the talk to praising Bharata.
Rama was afraid Kaikeyi's messengers might be listening somewhere in the forest.
Rama worried that Bharata would hear of it and come to the forest to punish Lakshmana.
chat.meaning: Rama said: don't speak badly of our middle mother, speak only of Bharata. He doesn't defend Kaikeyi; he refuses the bitterness.

hemanta.meaning: early winter, one of the traditional seasons of the Indian year

Godavari.meaning: the river by Panchavati where they bathe

Sarayu.meaning: the river of Ayodhya, Rama's home city

Kaikeyi.meaning: Bharata's mother, whose wish sent Rama into exile

Shatrughna.meaning: the fourth brother, close to Bharata

recall: the mountain of their first forest home

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 16 (the winter morning; Lakshmana on Bharata and Kaikeyi; Rama's reply)
